title: ‘Groundbreaking technology often enters the market at a premium before scaling’: Touch-sensitive e-skin…
excerpt: Electronic skin could give robots the sensation they’ve been missing.
content_html:
Despite mammoth advanced in artificial intelligence and computer vision, and a slew of humanoid robots either being piloted or hitting parts of the market, there’s still one major challenge that machines need to overcome.

It’s tactility, sensation, knowing how to hold an object. Picking up a strawberry, for example, a robot might not know how much pressure to apply, whether it’s secure, slipping, or about to be crushed. It’s something that we humans can feel through our skin, but it’s much harder to replicate on a machine level.

But it’s a work in progress, because there are companies out there like Touchlab who are working to give these skin-like characteristics to robots in a bid to make them more useful around the home, in care or in manufacturing. And it’s a lot more complex than we could ever imagine.

In Touchlab’s instance, it actually relies on quantum tunnelling technology to measure pressure, force and direction through a material that’s thinner than human skin, and with response times of less than a millisecond.

E-skin technology exists, but deployment is a challenge

Although the solution is laid out on the table, moving from pilot to production is a different ball game. Durability, reliability, affordability, adaptability… they’re all considerations that stand between theory and real-world use cases.

Touchlab is addressing some of these concerns with off-the-shelf components that already exist for established platforms, using bespoke engineering only where necessary.

It’s also seeking to reduce latency by bringing processing to the edge so that the robot only transmits the data necessary for the task, being that the e-skin can detect and collect huge amounts of micro-data.

With robots now rolling out across workplaces, care environments and, likely soon, homes, the ability to sense contact is becoming as important as the ability to see.

I speak with Touchlab’s team to understand how we can go from pilot to production in a realistic way.

  • Why do robots need the sense of touch, and how is Touchlab trying to achieve this?

Computer vision allows a robot to predict, but touch is what confirms. Without tactile feedback, robotics remains trapped in a classic paradox: a machine can calculate complex equations in milliseconds, yet struggle to pick up a strawberry, handle soft medical instruments, or turn a valve without either crushing the object or dropping it. Without tactile sensing, a robot is functionally numb.

Touchlab solves this by developing biomimetic electronic skin (e-skin) that is actually thinner than human skin. Powered by quantum tunneling technology, our e-skin measures 3D forces, direction, and pressure in real-time. Crucially, it detects incipient slip—meaning the robot senses that an object is beginning to slip before it actually drops, enabling instantaneous, sub-millisecond grip adjustments just like the human nervous system.

  • I tried the technology at Future Lab... I tried to control a robotic arm with haptic feedback and it felt a bit clunky with cables and restrictions. Why is it so hard to make it smoother?

Teleoperation is a classic engineering balancing act! First, there is a natural learning curve—controlling a high-degree-of-freedom robotic arm through a haptic glove isn't always intuitive on the very first attempt. It usually takes a bit of practice time and muscle memory to get the hang of the subtle force dynamics.

Second, running live demonstrations at high-traffic public events like Future Lab introduces specific hardware constraints. To ensure hundreds of visitors with completely different hand sizes can safely participate, setup requires universal-fit, heavy-duty tethered rigs and robust cabling.

Longer-term, our roadmap moves away from bulky, tethered operator suits entirely. By embedding our e-skin directly onto the robot and pairing it with onboard AI, the robot handles slip detection and dexterity autonomously—removing the need for an operator to wear restrictive physical gear.

  • Right now, the focus is on your proprietary robot fingertip tech. What's the plan going forward? Do you plan to license it or sell it as a finished product? How will you deal with various robotic architectures?

Every robot platform is unique—whether it’s a humanoid deployed into hazardous industrial environments or a cobot assisting nurses in hospital wards. Touchlab is uniquely positioned to design, develop, and manufacture bespoke tactile devices tailored to specific OEM architectures.

At the same time, we offer scalable, off-the-shelf tactile components that are pre-integrated (both electronically and mechanically) with a wide variety of popular robot end-effectors. We provide volume-based discounts alongside strategic hardware loan and collaboration programs for robotics companies aligned with our vision. Over the past seven years, we have become extremely adept at rapidly building reliable integrations to suit diverse customer requirements.

  • What are currently the biggest technological barriers Touchlab is encountering? What does the end game look like, and will we ever digitize our largest organ, the skin?

Our ultimate end game is for Touchlab’s tactile technology to become as ubiquitous as MEMS sensors— integrated into every commercial robot interacting with objects and humans. We envision full "finger-to-toe" tactile coverage powered by specialized edge computing and tactile orchestration software that mirrors the human somatosensory system.

Regarding barriers: the challenge isn't just technical; it's navigating western market adoption timelines for deeply transformative hardware. While digitizing human skin at scale presents manufacturing and durability hurdles, Touchlab can already deliver sensors matching or exceeding human-level spatial resolution, readout frequency, and sensitivity. The real task is packaging this capability into rugged, cost-effective formats ready for mass market deployment.

  • How is Touchlab designing the user interface to reduce operator fatigue during long shifts?

We focus on shared autonomy. Rather than forcing a human operator to manually sense and adjust every micro-force vector, our e-skin handles low-level reflexes (like slip prevention) locally on the robot. The human operator directs higher-level tasks, while the robot's tactile system autonomously maintains optimal grip— dramatically reducing both physical strain and cognitive fatigue.

  • High-density e-skin generates massive amounts of data. How do you handle bandwidth and network transfer without overloading systems?

High-density sensing does not automatically equal richer functional data, and often comes at the cost of hardware robustness. For our commercial products, we optimize spatial and temporal sensor density specifically for manipulation tasks, keeping data payloads lightweight.

For advanced R&D, we utilize distributed edge computing and are pioneering event-based asynchronous sampling in tactile sensing (similar to event-based vision cameras). Because our e-skin does not rely on heavy image-based data streams, it operates with extremely low latency and modest network bandwidth— making long-distance remote teleoperation surprisingly efficient.

  • Because e-skin can identify objects and textures, what protocols protect tactile data security and privacy?

Tactile data on its own does not contain personally identifiable information. However, when integrated with video, audio, and LiDAR streams, multi-modal data security becomes critical.

For example, during our deployment with the Valkky medical robot in a Finnish hospital, all data transferred across hospital networks was strictly encrypted. Identifiable multi-modal data remained entirely on-premises on air-gapped storage devices and was fully anonymized before being processed for research or system analytics.

  • E-skin is often seen as a high-end luxury. What is your roadmap for driving down production costs for commercial robotics?

Much like the early days of automobiles, groundbreaking technology often enters the market at a premium before scaling. While Touchlab is capable of producing full human-spec density today, deploying that level of complexity everywhere would make commercial robots cost-prohibitive.

Our strategy focuses on pragmatic engineering: delivering touch sensing tuned precisely to real-world task requirements at an accessible price point. We are actively collaborating with industry bodies to establish standardized performance metrics for tactile data, driving down manufacturing costs and making e-skin a standard baseline for all commercial robotics.

sentences.en: Touchlab is uniquely positioned to design, develop, and manufacture bespoke tactile devices tailored to specific OEM architectures.
sentences.zh: Touchlab 拥有独特的定位，可以设计、开发和制造针对特定 OEM 架构的定制触觉设备。

blocks.html_en: At the same time, we offer scalable, off-the-shelf tactile components that are pre-integrated (both electronically and mechanically) with a wide variety of popular robot end-effectors. We provide volume-based discounts alongside strategic hardware loan and collaboration programs for robotics companies aligned with our vision. Over the past seven years, we have become extremely adept at rapidly building reliable integrations to suit diverse customer requirements.

blocks.html_en: • What are currently the biggest technological barriers Touchlab is encountering? What does the end game look like, and will we ever digitize our largest organ, the skin?

sentences.en: What are currently the biggest technological barriers Touchlab is encountering?
sentences.zh: Touchlab目前遇到的最大技术障碍是什么？

sentences.en: What does the end game look like, and will we ever digitize our largest organ, the skin?
sentences.zh: 最终的游戏会是什么样子？我们是否会将我们最大的器官——皮肤数字化？

blocks.html_en: Our ultimate end game is for Touchlab’s tactile technology to become as ubiquitous as MEMS sensors— integrated into every commercial robot interacting with objects and humans. We envision full "finger-to-toe" tactile coverage powered by specialized edge computing and tactile orchestration software that mirrors the human somatosensory system.

sentences.en: Our ultimate end game is for Touchlab’s tactile technology to become as ubiquitous as MEMS sensors— integrated into every commercial robot interacting with objects and humans.
sentences.zh: 我们的最终目标是让 Touchlab 的触觉技术像 MEMS 传感器一样无处不在——集成到每个与物体和人类交互的商业机器人中。

sentences.en: We envision full "finger-to-toe" tactile coverage powered by specialized edge computing and tactile orchestration software that mirrors the human somatosensory system.
sentences.zh: 我们设想由专门的边缘计算和反映人类体感系统的触觉编排软件提供支持的完整“从手指到脚趾”的触觉覆盖。

blocks.html_en: Regarding barriers: the challenge isn't just technical; it's navigating western market adoption timelines for deeply transformative hardware. While digitizing human skin at scale presents manufacturing and durability hurdles, Touchlab can already deliver sensors matching or exceeding human-level spatial resolution, readout frequency, and sensitivity. The real task is packaging this capability into rugged, cost-effective formats ready for mass market deployment.

sentences.en: Regarding barriers: the challenge isn't just technical; it's navigating western market adoption timelines for deeply transformative hardware.

blocks.html_en: • How is Touchlab designing the user interface to reduce operator fatigue during long shifts?

sentences.en: How is Touchlab designing the user interface to reduce operator fatigue during long shifts?
sentences.zh: Touchlab 如何设计用户界面以减少操作员在长时间轮班期间的疲劳？

blocks.html_en: We focus on shared autonomy. Rather than forcing a human operator to manually sense and adjust every micro-force vector, our e-skin handles low-level reflexes (like slip prevention) locally on the robot. The human operator directs higher-level tasks, while the robot's tactile system autonomously maintains optimal grip— dramatically reducing both physical strain and cognitive fatigue.

sentences.en: We focus on shared autonomy.
sentences.zh: 我们专注于共享自主权。

sentences.en: Rather than forcing a human operator to manually sense and adjust every micro-force vector, our e-skin handles low-level reflexes (like slip prevention) locally on the robot.
sentences.zh: 我们的电子皮肤不是强迫人类操作员手动感应和调整每个微力矢量，而是在机器人上本地处理低级反射（例如防滑）。

sentences.en: The human operator directs higher-level tasks, while the robot's tactile system autonomously maintains optimal grip— dramatically reducing both physical strain and cognitive fatigue.
sentences.zh: 人类操作员指挥更高级别的任务，而机器人的触觉系统自动保持最佳抓地力，从而大大减轻身体压力和认知疲劳。

blocks.html_en: • High-density e-skin generates massive amounts of data. How do you handle bandwidth and network transfer without overloading systems?

sentences.en: High-density e-skin generates massive amounts of data.
sentences.zh: 高密度电子皮肤会产生大量数据。

sentences.en: How do you handle bandwidth and network transfer without overloading systems?
sentences.zh: 如何在不使系统过载的情况下处理带宽和网络传输？

blocks.html_en: High-density sensing does not automatically equal richer functional data, and often comes at the cost of hardware robustness. For our commercial products, we optimize spatial and temporal sensor density specifically for manipulation tasks, keeping data payloads lightweight.

sentences.en: High-density sensing does not automatically equal richer functional data, and often comes at the cost of hardware robustness.
sentences.zh: 高密度传感并不自动等于更丰富的功能数据，并且通常以硬件稳健性为代价。

sentences.en: For our commercial products, we optimize spatial and temporal sensor density specifically for manipulation tasks, keeping data payloads lightweight.
sentences.zh: 对于我们的商业产品，我们专门针对操作任务优化了空间和时间传感器密度，从而保持数据有效负载的轻量化。

blocks.html_en: For advanced R&D, we utilize distributed edge computing and are pioneering event-based asynchronous sampling in tactile sensing (similar to event-based vision cameras). Because our e-skin does not rely on heavy image-based data streams, it operates with extremely low latency and modest network bandwidth— making long-distance remote teleoperation surprisingly efficient.

sentences.en: For advanced R&D, we utilize distributed edge computing and are pioneering event-based asynchronous sampling in tactile sensing (similar to event-based vision cameras).
sentences.zh: 对于高级研发，我们利用分布式边缘计算，并在触觉传感领域开创了基于事件的异步采样（类似于基于事件的视觉相机）。

sentences.en: Because our e-skin does not rely on heavy image-based data streams, it operates with extremely low latency and modest network bandwidth— making long-distance remote teleoperation surprisingly efficient.
sentences.zh: 由于我们的电子皮肤不依赖于大量基于图像的数据流，因此它的运行延迟极低，网络带宽适中，使得长距离远程操作的效率出奇地高。

blocks.html_en: • Because e-skin can identify objects and textures, what protocols protect tactile data security and privacy?

sentences.en: Because e-skin can identify objects and textures, what protocols protect tactile data security and privacy?
sentences.zh: 由于电子皮肤可以识别物体和纹理，那么什么协议可以保护触觉数据的安全和隐私？

blocks.html_en: Tactile data on its own does not contain personally identifiable information. However, when integrated with video, audio, and LiDAR streams, multi-modal data security becomes critical.

sentences.en: Tactile data on its own does not contain personally identifiable information.
sentences.zh: 触觉数据本身不包含个人身份信息。

sentences.en: However, when integrated with video, audio, and LiDAR streams, multi-modal data security becomes critical.
sentences.zh: 然而，当与视频、音频和激光雷达流集成时，多模式数据安全性变得至关重要。

blocks.html_en: For example, during our deployment with the Valkky medical robot in a Finnish hospital, all data transferred across hospital networks was strictly encrypted. Identifiable multi-modal data remained entirely on-premises on air-gapped storage devices and was fully anonymized before being processed for research or system analytics.

sentences.en: For example, during our deployment with the Valkky medical robot in a Finnish hospital, all data transferred across hospital networks was strictly encrypted.

sentences.en: Identifiable multi-modal data remained entirely on-premises on air-gapped storage devices and was fully anonymized before being processed for research or system analytics.
sentences.zh: 可识别的多模式数据完全保留在本地气隙存储设备上，并且在进行研究或系统分析处理之前完全匿名。

blocks.html_en: Much like the early days of automobiles, groundbreaking technology often enters the market at a premium before scaling. While Touchlab is capable of producing full human-spec density today, deploying that level of complexity everywhere would make commercial robots cost-prohibitive.

We are actively collaborating with industry bodies to establish standardized performance metrics for tactile data, driving down manufacturing costs and making e-skin a standard baseline for all commercial robotics.

content_html_zh:
尽管人工智能和计算机视觉领域取得了巨大的进步，并且大量的人形机器人正在试用或进入部分市场，但机器仍然需要克服一个重大挑战。

它是触觉、感觉、知道如何握住物体。 例如，拿起草莓时，机器人可能不知道要施加多大的压力，无论它是安全的、打滑的还是即将被压碎。 这是我们人类可以通过皮肤感受到的东西，但在机器层面上复制要困难得多。

但这是一项正在进行的工作，因为像 Touchlab 这样的公司正在努力为机器人赋予这些类似皮肤的特性，以使它们在家庭、护理或制造领域更加有用。 它比我们想象的要复杂得多。

在 Touchlab 的例子中，它实际上依靠量子隧道技术来通过比人类皮肤还薄的材料来测量压力、力和方向，并且响应时间不到一毫秒。

电子皮肤技术已经存在，但部署是一个挑战

尽管解决方案已摆在桌面上，但从试点转向生产是另一回事。 耐用性、可靠性、经济性、适应性…… 它们都是介于理论和现实用例之间的考虑因素。

Touchlab 正在使用现有平台上现有的现成组件来解决其中一些问题，仅在必要时使用定制工程。

它还寻求通过将处理带到边缘来减少延迟，以便机器人仅传输任务所需的数据，因为电子皮肤可以检测和收集大量微数据。

随着机器人现在在工作场所、护理环境以及（可能很快）家庭中推广，感知接触的能力变得与视觉的能力一样重要。

我与 Touchlab 的团队进行了交谈，了解我们如何以现实的方式从试点转向生产。

  • 为什么机器人需要触觉，Touchlab 是如何实现这一目标的？

计算机视觉可以让机器人进行预测，但触摸可以进行确认。 如果没有触觉反馈，机器人技术仍然陷入一个经典的悖论：机器可以在几毫秒内计算出复杂的方程，但却很难在不压碎或掉落物体的情况下拿起草莓、处理柔软的医疗器械或转动阀门。 如果没有触觉感知，机器人的功能就会变得麻木。

Touchlab 通过开发实际上比人类皮肤更薄的仿生电子皮肤（e-skin）解决了这个问题。 我们的电子皮肤采用量子隧道技术，可实时测量 3D 力、方向和压力。 至关重要的是，它可以检测到初期的滑动，这意味着机器人在物体真正掉落之前就感觉到它开始滑动，从而能够像人类神经系统一样进行瞬时、亚毫秒级的抓握调整。

  • 我在未来实验室尝试了这项技术...... 我尝试用触觉反馈来控制机械臂，但由于电缆和限制，感觉有点笨重。 为什么让它变得更顺畅这么难？

远程操作是经典的工程平衡行为！ 首先，有一个自然的学习曲线——通过触觉手套控制高自由度的机械臂在第一次尝试时并不总是直观的。 通常需要一些练习时间和肌肉记忆才能掌握微妙的力动态。

其次，在未来实验室等高流量公共活动中进行现场演示会引入特定的硬件限制。 为了确保数百名手部尺寸完全不同的游客能够安全参与，设置需要通用型、重型系绳装置和坚固的电缆。

从长远来看，我们的路线图完全摆脱笨重、系绳的操作服。 通过将我们的电子皮肤直接嵌入到机器人上并将其与机载人工智能配对，机器人可以自主处理滑动检测和灵活性，从而消除了操作员佩戴限制性物理装备的需要。

  • 现在，重点是您专有的机器人指尖技术。 下一步有何计划？ 您打算授权它还是将其作为成品出售？ 您将如何处理各种机器人架构？

每个机器人平台都是独一无二的——无论是部署到危险工业环境中的人形机器人，还是在医院病房协助护士的协作机器人。 Touchlab 拥有独特的定位，可以设计、开发和制造针对特定 OEM 架构的定制触觉设备。

同时，我们提供可扩展的现成触觉组件，这些组件与各种流行的机器人末端执行器预先集成（电子和机械方式）。 我们为符合我们愿景的机器人公司提供基于数量的折扣以及战略硬件贷款和合作计划。 在过去的七年里，我们已经非常擅长快速构建可靠的集成，以满足不同的客户需求。

  • Touchlab目前遇到的最大技术障碍是什么？ 最终的游戏会是什么样子？我们是否会将我们最大的器官——皮肤数字化？

我们的最终目标是让 Touchlab 的触觉技术像 MEMS 传感器一样无处不在——集成到每个与物体和人类交互的商业机器人中。 我们设想由专门的边缘计算和反映人类体感系统的触觉编排软件提供支持的完整“从手指到脚趾”的触觉覆盖。

关于障碍：挑战不仅是技术上的，而且是技术上的。它正在遵循西方市场采用深度变革硬件的时间表。 虽然大规模数字化人类皮肤存在制造和耐用性障碍，但 Touchlab 已经可以提供匹配或超过人类水平空间分辨率、读出频率和灵敏度的传感器。 真正的任务是将这种功能封装成坚固耐用、经济高效的格式，为大众市场部署做好准备。

  • Touchlab 如何设计用户界面以减少操作员在长时间轮班期间的疲劳？

我们专注于共享自主权。 我们的电子皮肤不是强迫人类操作员手动感应和调整每个微力矢量，而是在机器人上本地处理低级反射（例如防滑）。 人类操作员指挥更高级别的任务，而机器人的触觉系统自动保持最佳抓地力，从而大大减轻身体压力和认知疲劳。

  • 高密度电子皮肤会产生大量数据。 如何在不使系统过载的情况下处理带宽和网络传输？

高密度传感并不自动等于更丰富的功能数据，并且通常以硬件稳健性为代价。 对于我们的商业产品，我们专门针对操作任务优化了空间和时间传感器密度，从而保持数据有效负载的轻量化。

对于高级研发，我们利用分布式边缘计算，并在触觉传感领域开创了基于事件的异步采样（类似于基于事件的视觉相机）。 由于我们的电子皮肤不依赖于大量基于图像的数据流，因此它的运行延迟极低，网络带宽适中，使得长距离远程操作的效率出奇地高。

  • 由于电子皮肤可以识别物体和纹理，那么什么协议可以保护触觉数据的安全和隐私？

触觉数据本身不包含个人身份信息。 然而，当与视频、音频和激光雷达流集成时，多模式数据安全性变得至关重要。

例如，在芬兰一家医院部署 Valkky 医疗机器人期间，通过医院网络传输的所有数据都经过严格加密。 可识别的多模式数据完全保留在本地气隙存储设备上，并且在进行研究或系统分析处理之前完全匿名。

  • 电子皮肤通常被视为高端奢侈品。 您降低商业机器人生产成本的路线图是什么？

就像早期的汽车一样，突破性技术在规模化之前通常会以溢价进入市场。 虽然 Touchlab 目前能够生产完全符合人类规格的密度，但在任何地方部署这种复杂程度将使商用机器人成本过高。

我们的战略侧重于务实的工程：以可承受的价格提供精确适应现实世界任务要求的触摸传感。 我们正在积极与行业机构合作，建立触觉数据的标准化性能指标，降低制造成本并使电子皮肤成为所有商业机器人的标准基准。

Désiré 在四十年的职业生涯中一直在思考和撰写有关技术的文章。 当 DHTML 和框架盛行时，他涉足网站建设和网络托管，并在上个世纪之交的“千年虫”歇斯底里开始之前开始讲述技术对社会的影响。
